_note: Step-by-step clues for Venn Diagrams (Chapter 32): the book questions and the past-paper questions filed under the chapter, by question id. Each list asks the student to take the groups two at a time (is every one of these also one of those, do some overlap, or have they nothing in common), gives the facts for this question, then asks which drawing shows them. For the survey questions it says which parts of the circles to add. The last clue never names the diagram. Questions marked needs-review have none. tools/check_clues.ts checks them.

vd-b01: Take the groups two at a time. For each pair ask: is every one of these also one of those (circle inside circle)? Are some both (circles overlap)? Or nothing in common (circles apart)?
Some animals eat both plants and meat, so Herbivorous and Carnivorous overlap. A dog eats both, so it goes in the overlap.
Draw that with circles. Which diagram matches your drawing?

vd-b10: Everyone inside the Coffee circle drinks coffee, including the part it shares with Tea.
The Coffee circle has two parts: coffee only, and both coffee and tea.
Add the numbers in those two parts. How many is that?
vd-b11: 'Only tea' means tea but not coffee.
That is the part of the Tea circle outside the Coffee circle.
Which number is in that part?
vd-b12: That is the part where the two circles overlap.
Which number is in that part?
